headline_en: A few days on the Mediterranean shore: Nice, Ventimiglia, Sanremo and Monaco
summary_en: A travel diary by a Bangladeshi-born Swedish citizen who travelled from Stockholm to Nice, Ventimiglia, Sanremo and Monaco from 1 June 2026. In the Italian border town of Ventimiglia he saw expatriate Bangladeshis' hard daily struggle with work pressure and limited opportunities, and Bangladeshi vegetables being grown there. The rest is travel reflection.

facts.statement: A Bangladeshi-born Swedish writer visiting Ventimiglia, an Italian hill-ringed border town, in early June 2026 wrote that expatriate Bangladeshis there live a hard life of work pressure, limited opportunities and constant effort to establish themselves, where every day is a kind of struggle.
The writer saw familiar Bangladeshi vegetables being cultivated in Ventimiglia, Italy, by Bangladeshis living there.
The writer, a Bangladeshi who is a Swedish citizen, said travelling by train between European countries (France to Italy) involved no separate long process, visa check or formal stop at the border.
Prothom Alo's 'Dur Porobash' section accepts stories, news, videos and photos of life abroad from readers at the email dp@prothomalo.com.

headline_en: 50 including women and children rescued in Teknaf, 9 traffickers arrested
summary_en: Bangladesh Coast Guard rescued 50 people, including women and children (39 Bangladeshis and 11 Rohingya), from a fishing trawler off Baharchhara on the Teknaf coast as they were being trafficked to Malaysia by sea on the evening of Friday 5 June 2026. Nine traffickers were arrested and handed to Teknaf Model Police Station with a case filed. The station in-charge said gangs lure people with promises of high-paid jobs abroad, then hold them in hideouts and torture them for ransom.

facts.statement: Bangladesh Coast Guard chased and seized a fishing trawler in the sea off Baharchhara on the Teknaf coast (Cox's Bazar) that was carrying people to Malaysia by sea, rescuing 50 victims including women and children and arresting 9 human traffickers.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Commander Md. Muttakin Siddiqui, in-charge of Coast Guard's Teknaf station, at a press conference on 6 June 2026

facts.statement: Of the 50 people rescued from the Malaysia-bound trawler off Teknaf, 11 were Rohingya and 39 were Bangladeshi nationals.

facts.statement: Trafficking route: people are taken to the Teknaf coast in Cox's Bazar and put on fishing trawlers to go to Malaysia by sea; when the Coast Guard signalled the trawler to stop, the traffickers tried to flee at speed.

Organised trafficking gangs lure Bangladeshi and Rohingya people to the Teknaf coast with promises of high-paid jobs abroad and a better life, then lock them in secret hideouts and extract ransom through torture.
facts.source_in_article: Lt Commander Md. Muttakin Siddiqui, Coast Guard

facts.statement: The nine arrested alleged traffickers, Md. Russell (Rasel), Md. Amir Uddin, Md. Sahabuddin, Md. Yunus, Md. Jasim, Md. Rafiq, Md. Abdur Razzak, Md. Ismail and Md. Suruj Zaman, were handed to Teknaf Model Police Station and a case was filed under the relevant law.

Bangladeshi youth killed in attack in Iraq buried two and a half months later
summary_en: Md. Shrabon alias Hobi Mia (35) of Bakultala, Munshiganj Sadar, who had worked in Baghdad as an irregular migrant since going to Iraq in 2016, was killed in a missile attack in Baghdad on 14 March 2026. His body reached Dhaka on a Turkish Airlines flight under government arrangement on 29 May 2026, about two and a half months later, with help from local administration and the Bangladesh embassy, and was buried the same day. His widow asked the government for a house on his village land so their two daughters can keep studying.

facts.statement: Bangladeshi worker Md. Shrabon alias Hobi Mia (35), of Bakultala village, Adhara union, Munshiganj Sadar, was killed in a missile attack in Baghdad, Iraq, on 14 March 2026.
Md. Shrabon went to Iraq in 2016 and had worked for several years in Baghdad as an irregular (undocumented) migrant; he had not come home in about 10 years.
Shrabon's family learned of his 14 March 2026 death in Baghdad on 16 March, when a co-worker phoned his wife Khadija Akter.

Shrabon's body was flown to Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka, at 5:15 am on 29 May 2026 on a Turkish Airlines flight under government management, and handed to the family after all legal procedures; this was about two and a half months after his death.
The return of Shrabon's body from Iraq was arranged with the cooperation of Munshiganj local administration and the Bangladesh embassy, even though he was working in Iraq irregularly.

In his last phone call with his wife on 13 March 2026, Shrabon described a terrifying situation of missile attacks all around in Baghdad and said he would come home when the war ended and not go abroad again.

Shrabon's widow Khadija Akter, who has two daughters (Habiba Akter, 16, and Nafiza Akter, 10), said the family has no means and asked for the government to build a house on his village land so the girls can continue their studies.

Bangladeshis in Spain get direct police clearance service
summary_en: A special Home Ministry team led by Deputy Secretary Kazi Arifur Rahman gave Bangladeshi migrants in Spain police clearance certificates directly, for the first time in any European country. About 600 people were served in Barcelona from 9 to 11 May 2026, and the service was extended to the Madrid embassy on 14, 17, 18 and 19 May. Speakers said police clearance is an essential document for Spain's amnesty to regularise about 500,000 undocumented migrants.

facts.statement: A special delegation of Bangladesh's Ministry of Home Affairs, led by Deputy Secretary Kazi Arifur Rahman, gave police clearance certificates directly to Bangladeshi migrants in Spain; in the first phase in Barcelona, from 9 to 11 May 2026, about six hundred-plus (ছয় শতাধিক) expatriates received the service.
According to related sources, this was the first time the Bangladesh government provided police clearance directly in any European country.

In Barcelona the police clearance service ran daily from 10 am to 5 pm in a hall room in the Josep Tarradellas (জোসেফ তারাদিয়া) area; for new online applicants, the certificate was handed over on the spot after their information was verified.
The Home Ministry team in Spain also corrected errors in old police clearance certificates and settled long-stuck offline applications quickly by having them re-filed as new online applications.

The special police clearance service, which started on 9 May and was to run until 13 May across Barcelona and Madrid, was extended due to heavy demand; under the new decision it was to be given in the hall room of the Bangladesh Embassy in Madrid on 14, 17, 18 and 19 May 2026.

Spain's government recently announced an amnesty ('general pardon') to regularise about five lakh (500,000) undocumented migrants in the country, and a police clearance certificate is an essential document for it.
facts.source_in_article: speakers at a Spain BNP thanksgiving meeting in Barcelona, 9 May 2026

facts.statement: People involved said the special police clearance service saved Bangladeshi migrants in Spain time and money, and speakers said getting it on time made it easier for thousands of Bangladeshis to become legal.
Bangladesh's ambassador to Spain, Masudur Rahman, was chief guest at a short thanksgiving meeting held by Spain BNP in Barcelona on 9 May 2026 for the police clearance service.

headline_en: Demand to post police officers at some embassies abroad
summary_en: At a Police Week 2026 event at Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's office on 11 May 2026, senior police officers asked for police officers to be posted as liaison officers and legal attachés at Bangladesh embassies in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Dubai, Italy, Singapore and Malaysia, to help expatriates quickly and to recover laundered money via Interpol. They also asked for police to be posted again at the Department of Immigration and Passports. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said work is under way to deliver police clearance certificates and online GDs faster and ordered that past complaints of harassment over police clearance must not recur.

facts.statement: At a Police Week 2026 event at the Prime Minister's office on 11 May 2026, a senior Police Headquarters officer told PM Tarique Rahman that very large numbers of Bangladeshis work in Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Dubai, Italy, Singapore and Malaysia, and asked that police officers be posted to Bangladesh embassies there as liaison officers and legal attachés so expatriates' problems can get immediate help.
facts.source_in_article: police sources; a senior Police Headquarters officer

facts.statement: The senior police officer said posting police officers at embassies in those seven countries would also make it easier to recover money laundered out of Bangladesh through Interpol.
Police said police officers used to work in the Department of Immigration and Passports (পাসপোর্ট অধিদপ্তর) but none do now, and asked that police officers be posted there again.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said work is under way to provide citizen services such as police clearance certificates and online GDs (general diaries) quickly, and ordered police to ensure that the complaints of harassment over police clearance seen in the past do not come again.
The Home Minister said a new decision assigns joint operations in border and coastal areas: BGB, river police and Coast Guard in border areas, and the Navy at sea.

The Home Minister said integrated laws and institutions are urgently needed against money laundering, digital fraud and telecom-based crime, proposed a separate cyber crime unit in Bangladesh Police, and said a high-level committee is drafting a new law on cyber crime, false information and propaganda.
Police HQ spokesman AIG (Media and PR) A H M Shahadat Hossain said the PM listened to the police demands and the Home Minister assured that some needs would be met.
facts.source_in_article: AIG A H M Shahadat Hossain

headline_en: BSF returns two Bangladeshis caught at Thakurgaon border while returning home illegally
summary_en: India's Border Security Force (BSF) detained two Bangladeshis at about midnight on Monday 27 April 2026 as they tried to come home without passports through the Boirchuna border in Pirganj, Thakurgaon. After a BGB-BSF flag meeting on 28 April they were handed to BGB, which handed them to Pirganj police; police said they will be sent to court after legal procedures.

facts.statement: A patrol of the BSF's Puranganon (পুরানগাঁও) camp, inside India, detained two Bangladeshis at the zero line of the Boirchuna (বৈরচুনা) border in Pirganj upazila, Thakurgaon, as they were trying to enter Bangladesh without passports.

BSF's Puranganon camp contacted the Boirchuna BOP (BGB border outpost); a flag meeting between the two camp commanders was held at a place called Dopail from 12:30 to 1:30 pm on 28 April 2026, after which BSF handed the two men to BGB.

BGB handed the two returnees, Majedur Rahman (36) of South Boirchuna, Pirganj, Thakurgaon, and Rana Sardar (31) of Bansbaria, Raninagar, Naogaon, to Pirganj police station; police said they would be sent to court after the necessary legal process for coming home without a passport.
facts.source_in_article: Inspector (investigation) Abdul Hakim, Pirganj police station

Expatriate entrepreneurs cited delays in approvals, land, utility connections, tax benefits and repatriating profits. facts.statement: Expatriate entrepreneurs in Los Angeles said complications and delays in post-investment approvals, land allocation, electricity and gas connections, tax benefits and repatriating profits are major challenges to investing in Bangladesh.

headline_en: Father's only wish: that US law enforcement finds Bristi's body
summary_en: Bangladeshi PhD student Nahida Sultana Bristi, murdered in Florida, had still not been found by US police as of 26 April 2026; her father asked US law enforcement to find her body and send it to Bangladesh. She had gone to the University of South Florida on a full scholarship on 25 August 2025. Madaripur's deputy commissioner said the family must submit an application, which the district will forward to the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry to arrange bringing the body home once police find it. Fellow student Jamil Ahmed Limon's body was found on Friday 24 April and his roommate Hisham Saleh Abugharbeh (26), a US citizen, was arrested.

facts.statement: Two Bangladeshi PhD students at the University of South Florida (USF) in Tampa, Florida, Jamil Ahmed Limon (geography, environmental science and policy) and Nahida Sultana Bristi (chemical engineering), went missing from 17 April 2026; both were last seen on campus on the Thursday before.

US police recovered Jamil's mutilated body from the Howard Frankland Bridge in Tampa, Florida, as announced by the Hillsborough local law enforcement agency at a press conference; Bristi's body had not been found as of 26 April 2026, though police found a body part at Limon's residence believed to be hers, without confirming.
facts.source_in_article: Hillsborough law enforcement; Bristi's father Jahir Uddin Akon

facts.statement: Local police arrested Hisham Saleh Abugharbeh, a 26-year-old US citizen who shared a room with Jamil, at his family home, over the disappearance of the two Bangladeshi students.

Bristi's father said the Bangladesh embassy in the US, Bangladesh's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Florida police and the Bangladeshi community in the US were keeping regular contact with the family and promised help to find the body and ensure the killers' maximum punishment.
facts.source_in_article: father Jahir Uddin Akon alias Dil Mohammad

facts.statement: To bring home the body of a Bangladeshi who died abroad (here a student in the US), the family must submit an application to the district administration; Madaripur's deputy commissioner said the district would then send it to the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare (প্রবাসীকল্যাণ মন্ত্রণালয়) to take all steps including bringing the body home, once police find it.

Nahida Sultana Bristi, of Char Gobindapur, Khoajpur union, Madaripur Sadar (family living in Mirpur, Dhaka), left Dhaka for the US on 25 August 2025 after getting a full scholarship for a PhD at the University of South Florida; she had a BSc in chemistry and chemical engineering from Noakhali Science and Technology University and had enrolled in a master's at BUET before leaving.

headline_en: Body of one of two missing Bangladeshi students in the US recovered
summary_en: Police found the body of Jamil Ahmed Limon (27), a Bangladeshi PhD student at the University of South Florida missing for 10 days, at the Howard Frankland Bridge area after questioning his roommate Hisham Abugharbeh (26), who was arrested. Fellow Bangladeshi PhD student Nahida S. Bristi was still being searched for. Both were last seen on 16 April; a family friend reported them missing on 17 April.

facts.statement: The Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office said it recovered the body of Bangladeshi student Jamil Ahmed Limon (27), a PhD student in geography, environmental science and policy at the University of South Florida, from the Howard Frankland Bridge area in Florida after questioning his roommate.
Police arrested Hisham Abugharbeh (26), Jamil's roommate, over the case of the two missing Bangladeshi students.

According to the University of South Florida police department, Jamil was last seen around 9 am on 16 April 2026 at his dormitory near the university, and Nahida (chemical engineering PhD) around 10 am the same day at the university's Natural and Environmental Sciences building.
A family friend who could not reach Jamil and Nahida informed the authorities on 17 April 2026; two missing-person reports were filed and police began investigating.

Golam Mortoza, press minister at the Bangladesh Embassy in Washington, announced on Facebook that police recovered Jamil Limon's body after questioning a suspect and that nothing was yet known about Nahida S. Bristi, with the investigation ongoing.
facts.source_in_article: Press Minister Golam Mortoza, Facebook post

headline_en: 2025 was the deadliest year for Rohingya sea journeys: UNHCR
summary_en: UNHCR says about 900 Rohingya refugees went missing or died in the Andaman Sea and Bay of Bengal in 2025, the deadliest year on record for sea journeys in South and South-East Asia; one in seven of the 6,500-plus who attempted the crossing died or went missing. Overcrowded, unseaworthy boats usually leave Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh or Rakhine in Myanmar for Indonesia or Malaysia. A boat that left Bangladesh on 26 March 2026 sank with about 250 missing; only 9 were rescued near the Andaman Islands on 9 April.

facts.statement: About 900 Rohingya refugees went missing or died in the Andaman Sea and Bay of Bengal in 2025, the deadliest year in the history of sea journeys in South and South-East Asia.
More than 6,500 Rohingya tried to cross the sea in 2025, and one in every seven died or went missing; UNHCR says this route has the highest death rate of all refugee sea routes in the world.
More than 2,800 Rohingya had taken the dangerous sea journey in 2026 up to 13 April; in recent years more than half of those crossing have been women and children.

Overloaded, unseaworthy boats carrying Rohingya usually set off from Cox's Bazar in Bangladesh or Rakhine State in Myanmar bound for Indonesia or Malaysia, despite risks of trafficking, abuse and death at sea.

An overloaded boat that left Bangladesh by sea on 26 March 2026 sank in rough seas in the Andaman Sea; about 250 people went missing and only 9 were rescued alive near the Andaman Islands on 9 April 2026; UNHCR is giving the survivors medical and mental health care.

There are more than 13 lakh Rohingya refugees in the region, 12 lakh of them sheltered in Bangladesh; the 2025 joint humanitarian response received only 53 percent of the required funds, and lack of funds, insecurity in camps and no education or jobs push Rohingya onto the sea route.

headline_en: Bangladesh-India relations: in search of peace and dignity
Over 150 Bangladeshi students stuck at home over Kyrgyz visa problems
summary_en: More than 150 Bangladeshi medical students enrolled in Kyrgyzstan have been stuck in Bangladesh since July 2025 because Kyrgyzstan stopped approving their visas without warning or reason, even though the student category shows as open on the Kyrgyz visa portal. They have lost a full semester and face expulsion. At a 6 April 2026 press conference in Dhaka they asked for the PM's intervention, a special visa approval route for continuing students, and a Bangladesh embassy or consular section in Kyrgyzstan; Bangladesh has no embassy there (students use the embassy in Uzbekistan) and Kyrgyzstan has none in Bangladesh (visas go via its embassy in New Delhi).

facts.statement: More than 150 Bangladeshi medical students studying in Kyrgyzstan have been stuck in Bangladesh since July 2025 due to visa problems; the Kyrgyz government stopped granting them visas without any advance warning.
facts.source_in_article: stranded students' written statement at press conference, Dhaka Press Club, 6 April 2026

facts.statement: The Kyrgyz visa portal shows the student visa category as 'open', but Bangladeshi students' applications are not being approved, with no specific reason given.

Bangladeshi students in Kyrgyzstan who came home briefly (a normal practice for international students) found their visa applications for returning blocked without explanation; they have lost a full semester and face expulsion from their universities.
Student Sadhril Huda said he applied to extend his Kyrgyz visa before it expired but it was not extended; he was told to apply for a new visa, but that application is also not being accepted.

Bangladesh has no embassy in Kyrgyzstan; Bangladeshi students handle education-related visa work through the Bangladesh embassy in Uzbekistan. Kyrgyzstan has no embassy in Bangladesh; Kyrgyz visa work is done through the Kyrgyz embassy in New Delhi, India.

Students said that despite a visit to Kyrgyzstan by Bangladesh's ambassador, no effective solution came; they demanded the PM's intervention, a special visa approval route for continuing students, and an embassy or responsible consular section in Kyrgyzstan.
